role: Vice President — Governmental Relations, Continental Telephone Corporation
summary: William Friedman, representing Continental Telephone Corporation, expresses concern that the Executive Order and implementing regulations could inadvertently impede utility companies from accessing their authorized communications facilities on public lands. He hopes the regulations are intended to govern recreational ORV use only, and proposes that utility vehicles performing maintenance of authorized facilities be explicitly exempted from permit requirements. He also requests that any permit process clearly identify which federal land management agency holds transit authority over specific parcels.

statement.text:
1800 K Street, N.W. Washington, D. C. 20006 (202) 466-2895
William Friedman
Vice President — Governmental Relations
August 3, 1972
, 31
Mr. James Watt, Director Bureau of Outdoor Recreation Department of Interior Washington, D. C. 20240
Re: Departmental Implementation of Executive Order 11644, Use of Off Road Vehicles (ORV) on Public Lands
Dear Mr. Watt:
Continental Telephone Corporation is the third largest independent telephone company in the United States. In our operations we have a number of installations which are located on public lands and require off road access.
We have followed with interest the subject Executive Order and the Draft Environmental Statement prepared by your office and published on May 26, 1972. We are obviously affected by any instructions which may be published on this matter. We are advised by your Mr. Stuart Davey and Mr. William Honore that an implementing order is soon to be published, but prior to its publication, they suggested we send you any comments that we may have.
As we can interpret, neither the Executive Order nor your draft memorandum specifically consider the problem of expressly permitting the use of vehicles off established roadways for the purpose of maintaining authorized communication (and other utilities) facilities without first requiring that a permit be obtained. We would hope that the intent of the Executive Order and Environmental Statement is to regulate pleasure off-road vehicles, and not to impede the servicing of communications equipment. Accordingly, you might wish to consider including a statement such as: "Vehicles belonging to utility companies performing maintenance of authorized facilities on public lands may transit those lands without permit."
Further, may we suggest that any regulation which does require permits establish the procedure of obtaining its permits and the mechanism for determining what federal land management agency will be exercising transit authority over a particular piece of federal land on which we may have to operate.
We trust that these comments may be of use to you. We would be pleased to discuss this further with you if you desire.
Very truly yours,
William Friedman
